## Still live on `main` at `c1006ed8e` — and ⛔ the card's path is wrong

⚠️ First correction, because you would lose time on it: the card and triage both write `PermissionAdvancedFacets.tsx` as living under `inspectors/`. **It does not.** The file is `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PermissionAdvancedFacets.tsx` — no `inspectors/` segment. Read at `c1006ed8e`:

| line | reading |
|---|---|
| `:280`–`:281` | `const setScope = (patch: Partial<AdminScope>) => setDraft((p) => ({ ...p, adminScope: { ...asObject(p.adminScope), ...patch } }));` — unconditional key-by-key merge, exactly as filed |
| `:519` | the `businessUnit` input — `setScope({ businessUnit: e.target.value })` |
| `:527` | **Include subtree** — `setScope({ includeSubtree: !!v })`, reachable with `businessUnit` unset |
| `:544` | the three manage-\* switches — `setScope({ [key]: !!v })`, same |
| `:509` | the badge — `count={scope.businessUnit \|\| (scope.assignablePermissionSets?.length ?? 0) ? 1 : 0}` ⇒ reads `0` for a draft that already blocks Save |

## ⛔ THE SHAPE IS SET HERE, AND TRIAGE SAYS SO EXPLICITLY

Triage declined to rule it and handed it to this seat: 「填报席列了四种修法(剪键 / 禁用从属控件 / 客户端校验 / 改徽标口径)—— 它们在**权限面**上并不等价(「剪键」会静默丢掉作者已拨的开关)。**定型归派发时的车道边界**,⛔ 分诊席不裁。」 So this is my call and I am making it rather than passing the fork to you:

- ⛔ **PRUNE IS OUT.** Dropping the key when the scope reduces to one without a `businessUnit` silently discards switches the author deliberately flipped. Triage names that cost; a permission editor that quietly un-does an author's input is a worse defect than the one on the card.
- ✅ **The defect has two halves and BOTH are in scope.** (i) An invalid `adminScope` can be written at all; (ii) the collapsed badge reads `0` and points the author **away** from the section that caused it. A fix that closes only (i) leaves an author who already has such a draft stranded; a fix that closes only (ii) leaves the trap armed.
- ✅ **Close (i) at the source** — the dependent controls do not write a scope until `businessUnit` names one. Disabled-with-a-reason is the shape I expect; if your reading says a client-side parse surfacing the error in the section is better on this surface, **argue it from the measurement and take it** — that is the one substitution I am pre-authorising, because it closes (i) without discarding input either.
- ✅ **Close (ii)** by making the badge count a scope that is non-empty, so a section carrying state never reports that it carries none.

⛔ If you conclude both halves cannot be closed without a maintainer ruling, **stop and report** — do not land half.

## ⛔ Hard constraints

- ⛔ **objectui#7265 is NOT a regression suspect.** Triage: 「该卡只让分歧**可见**,⛔ 不是它引入的 —— 前后行为逐字相同,⛔ 不要当作回归查」. Do not bisect it and do not reopen it.
- ⛔ **Do not touch `@objectstack/spec`.** `AdminScopeSchema` is correct — `businessUnit` required, the other five `ZodDefault` — and it is another repo. The editor is what is wrong.
- ⛔ **Do not widen the editor's accepted shapes** to make the bad draft legal. The repair stops the invalid write; it does not relax the contract.
- ⛔ objectui `AGENTS.md:316`: never `git push --force` or `--force-with-lease`, never push to `main`. Absolute, and ⛔ **not** tiered by seat.
- ⚠️ Scope-pinned card ⇒ AGENTS.md #11's opportunistic citation repair does **not** apply.

## Clause-②: `no` — measured

| probe | reading |
|---|---|
| SUBJECT — `PermissionAdvancedFacets` named in `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts` | **0 hits** |
| CONTROL — the entry is not empty | **84** `^export` lines |
| CONTROL — the entry reaches this very directory | 25 named `metadata-admin` leaf re-exports at `:371`–`:428`; this file is **absent** from them |
| the file's own exports | `:173` `export interface PermissionAdvancedFacetsProps`, `:197` the component, `:588` a default — module-level, not entry-level |

⚠️ Re-measure at delivery and return `clause_2`. ⭐ Trap warning, and I hit its mirror image an hour ago on a sibling card: *"not named in the package entry" is not the same as "not on the published face"* — a type referenced by any exported signature reaches the published `.d.ts`. If your diff touches anything reachable that way, clause ② flips ⇒ stop and report.

## The pin

It must **fail on the pre-fix tree** and it must go through the **editor**, not through `AdminScopeSchema` alone — a pin that only re-asserts the card's `safeParse` readings measures the spec, which is not what is broken. Drive it: mount the facet with `adminScope` unset, toggle **Include subtree**, and assert (a) what the draft now carries, and (b) what the badge reads. ⭐ Keep the card's positive control lit in the same file: `AdminScopeSchema.safeParse({ businessUnit: 'bu_sales' })` succeeds, so a `false` on the other leg is a reading about the payload and not about a broken import.

## Serial constraints cleared

`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/` — I read the changed-file list of all 9 open PRs; none touches `metadata-admin`. ⚠️ **One sibling of mine is in the same directory tree**: PR objectui#9775 (card objectui#9382) changes `views/metadata-admin/inspectors/datasetFilterCondition.ts` and its tests — a **different file**, and it is awaiting review rather than in flight. ⛔ Named rather than assumed; merge `main` before you open your PR, and again if objectui#9775 lands while you are in flight. ⛔ Never hand-order around it; the queue arbitrates.

## Return

The driven pre-fix red through the editor with the control lit, which of the two substitutions you took for half (i) and why, the badge reading before and after, the `clause_2` field, and any premise of mine you falsified — ⭐ the card's own file path was already one of them. **A clean stop is a full success.**

    Fixes #9464
    
    `AdminScopeSchema` makes `businessUnit` the one REQUIRED key — the other five carry
    defaults — so `{ includeSubtree: true }` is refused wholesale. `PermissionAdvancedFacets`
    patched the draft key by key from every control in the Delegated Admin Scope section, so
    flipping **Include subtree**, any of the three manage-\* switches, or picking an assignable
    permission set *before* naming a business unit wrote exactly that object. There is no
    client-side parse of the facet before Save, so the refusal landed as a server error on the
    author's next whole-record Save — of a record they may have been editing for entirely
    unrelated reasons.
    
    The collapsed badge made it hard to self-diagnose: it counted `businessUnit` and
    `assignablePermissionSets` only, so a draft that had just blocked Save reported
    "nothing configured here" and pointed the author away from the section that caused it.
    
    ## What changed
    
    **(i) at the source.** The dependent controls write through a gated `setScopeDetail` and
    carry the same `disabled` condition, with the reason named in the section
    (`perm.admin.businessUnitRequired`, `en` + `zh`). While no business unit names a subtree
    root they write nothing. The business-unit input keeps the ungated writer — it is what
    lifts the gate. The assignable-set buttons are gated too: they were the same trap on the
    one path whose badge already read `1`.
    
    **(ii) the badge.** It now counts any scope the draft carries, so a section holding state
    never reports that it holds none — including a draft that already carries an unsaveable
    scope from before this change.
    
    **Nothing is pruned.** A scope already carrying flipped switches keeps every one of them.
    Prune was ruled out on dispatch because it silently discards switches the author
    deliberately flipped; an already-poisoned draft is recovered by naming the business unit
    its switches were always missing.
    
    ### Why the gate rather than a client-side parse
    
    Both shapes were pre-authorised. The gate was taken on the reading, not on preference:
    
    - A client-side parse **does not close half (i) as filed** — the invalid object is still
      written into the draft on the same click; only its visibility changes. Closing (i)
      through a parse needs the verdict reported up so the host can gate Save, which is a
      second decision on `PermissionAdvancedFacetsProps` and on `PermissionMatrixEditor`.
    - It would add `AdminScopeSchema` as a **runtime** import to a file that today imports
      from `@objectstack/spec` as a type only, and run a zod parse on every keystroke of the
      business-unit input.
    - The gate keeps the diagnosis a parse would have bought: the section names the reason,
      and the badge points at itself.
    
    The gate's own condition is a business unit that *names* something (trimmed, non-empty),
    which is strictly narrower than the spec's requirement that the key merely be present.
    The error tone tracks the spec's condition instead, because that is the one that refuses
    the record.
    
    ## Evidence
    
    Pre-fix RED, driven through the editor (not against the schema), on the tree before the
    fix commit — 5 failed / 4 passed:
    
    ```
    AssertionError: the editor wrote {"includeSubtree":true}, which the spec refuses: expected false to be true
    AssertionError: expected { manageAssignments: true, …(2) } to be undefined
    AssertionError: expected { Object (assignablePermissionSets) } to be undefined
    TestingLibraryElementError: Unable to find an element with the text: perm.admin.businessUnitRequired
    TestingLibraryElementError: Unable to find an element with the text: 1   (the badge, for a draft carrying {includeSubtree:true})
    ```
    
    The card's controls stayed lit through both runs, which is what makes the `false` above a
    reading about the payload and not about a broken import:
    `AdminScopeSchema.safeParse({ businessUnit: 'bu_sales' }).success === true`, and
    `safeParse({ includeSubtree: true })` refuses on path `businessUnit`.
    
    Post-fix, at `6d883ea26`:
    
    | run | result |
    |---|---|
    | the new pin, `--project dom` | 9 passed |
    | `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/` (whole directory) | 264 files, 2825 passed, 1 skipped |
    | every test outside that directory that reaches either changed module | 74 files, 1198 passed |
    | `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (`tsc --noEmit` + `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) | exit 0 |
    | `eslint` over the three changed files, repo flags | 0 errors |
    
    The out-of-directory set is the enumerated reach of the diff, not a sample: every test that
    imports `PermissionAdvancedFacets` / `PermissionMatrixEditor`, plus every test that imports
    the `metadata-admin` i18n table. It includes `spec-symbol-parity.test.ts`, which pins this
    editor's `AdminScope` against the spec's in both directions.
    
    Gates run locally, all exit 0: `check:control-bytes`, `check:i18n-designer-parity`,
    `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-dead-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:changeset-claims`,
    `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:test-path-roots`,
    `check:unreferenced-sources`. `check:governed-queue-guard --test` reports NOT GOVERNED for
    all four changed paths.
    
    Repo-wide `eslint .` and the full-farm gate set are CI's run, not this branch's.
    
    ## Acceptance notes
    
    Noted while in this file, deliberately **not** fixed here and **not** filed:
    
    - This editor still has no way to REMOVE an `adminScope` once a draft carries one — no
      control deletes keys, and prune is ruled out. An author who wants *no* delegated admin
      scope has no path through this section; the recovery this change gives them is to name
      the business unit their switches were missing. The gap predates the card and is
      unchanged by this branch. No queued pull request touches this file.
    - `AdminScopeSchema.businessUnit` is `z.string()` with no minimum, so
      `{ businessUnit: '' }` and `{ businessUnit: '   ' }` both parse green (measured against
      the resolved pin, `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0). That is another repository and the card
      fences it off; it is reported upward rather than acted on here. This branch's own gate
      is stricter than the schema, so the dependent controls never author it.
